question: Different cell organelles such as mitochondria, ribosome, etc., together constitute the basic unit of life called the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life in all living organisms.
 
• Organelles such as mitochondria, ribosomes, and others are components within a cell that perform specific functions necessary for the cell's survival and operation.
 
• The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes, including metabolism, growth, and reproduction.
 
• Cells can be prokaryotic (without a nucleus, e.g., bacteria) or eukaryotic (with a nucleus, e.g., plant and animal cells).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**: Known as the powerhouse of the cell, mitochondria generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• **Ribosomes**: These are the sites of protein synthesis, where RNA is translated into protein.
 
• **Nucleus**: The control center of a eukaryotic cell, containing most of the cell's genetic material.
 
• **Cell Membrane**: A biological membrane that separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment, providing protection and structure.
 
• **Cytoplasm**: The material within a cell, excluding the nucleus, which contains organelles and is the site of many metabolic processes.
